newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crude edges up, ANS trade thins.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crude edges up, ANS trade thins.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crudes were bid slightly higher midday, tracking gains in West Texas Intermediate (WTI) amid a lack of Alaskan deals, traders said.
Early WTI trade saw bids up five cents to $26.05 a barrel. The slight rise combined with flat discounts left Alaska North Slope (ANS) bids at $24.30, or five cents over Wednesday.
Offers were flat at $24.45 a barrel.

A trading house broker saw BP lowering its ANS discount five cents to $1.65 under WTI. BP wants to drop prices before the close of January business because they have failed to capture recent spreads for the next month, he said.
"I would expect the next deal done to be $1.65," the dealer said.
A major ANS refiner led bids with a minus $2.25 price, traders said.
Line 63 crude was thin, with no fixed basis deals and posted plus values stagnant at $0.95 to $1.05.
Kern River prices stayed $18.15/18.25 a barrel late after rising Monday on increased posted prices.
Discounts remained 10 cents below to even with postings, traders said.
Wilmington crude, produced offshore in Long Beach, Calif., also rose with postings Monday to $19.65/19.75.
